provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `Sanctorum Martyrum tuorum` where 1862 reads `SAnct6rum Mdrtyrum tu6rum`; 1962 reads `Sergii,` where 1862 reads `S6rgii`; 1962 has nothing there; 1862 has `:`; 1962 reads `faciant amore ferventes. Per Dominum.` where 1862 reads `fticiant am6re ferv6ntes.`; 1862 sets no comma after the first of the four names and one after the third; the 1962 reverses that pointing; 1862 prints no conclusion, because it prints the prayer as a commemoration inside another Mass; the 1962 prints the short cue; 1862 layer damages one verb (`fticiant`); the letters either side fix it and the 1962 reads it plainly. Corroboration: 1922 Mame carries these martyrs at PDF pp. 845-847; not transcribed.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Sanctorum Martyrum tuorum nos, Domine, Sergii, Bacchi, Marcelli et Apuleii
beata merita prosequantur: et tuo semper faciant amore ferventes. Per
Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
